story: Gary is quietly testing a labeled speaker module in his workshop at low volume, leaving his golf cart untouched. On Magnolia Loop, Donna is standing firm about her flamingos, insisting she has three in view and that any Halloween decorations are staying in the garage, while Hal admits with some embarrassment that he's been counting them himself. Rosa sits on the bench in Town Square, reviewing the parade plan for Saturday and enjoying the warm, hazy evening before she heads home.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Quietly test the labeled speaker module at low volume, cart left untouched
Rosa waited: Resting on the bench, going over Saturday's parade plan and enjoying the warm hazy evening before heading home.

gary.thought_process: I'm home alone at the workbench, and it's getting late. The wiring is soldered and labeled, but the cart is still untouched in the garage because the Architectural Review application isn't signed off (L-01). I want this done the honest way. The speaker module should get a quiet bench test before 10 PM (L-03), and low volume keeps me well within the rules. Testing on the bench isn't modifying the cart, so it's fine. Then I'll call it a night and wait on the committee.

parameters.content: Quietly test the labeled speaker module at low volume, cart left untouched

donna.thought_process: Gary never showed at the court, so I walked back to the Loop. Hal is right here and he's the one who counts my flamingos, with the Halloween decorating week starting. Better to check in with him now and show I'm meeting the code rather than fighting it. I'll keep it friendly and quick, then see about tracking down Gary for tomorrow's practice.

parameters.content: Evening, Hal! Go ahead and count the flamingos if you like, I'm holding at three visible from the street, and any Halloween extras stay in the garage. Have you seen Gary around? He stood me up on the court.

hal.thought_process: Donna just walked up while I'm standing here by her flamingo flock. I've already warned her straight, and I've been counting these birds like a man with nothing better to do. My reflections say I'm getting more invested in being right than in being neighborly. L-02 caps ornaments at three, and I'm not pretending that isn't the rule, but a neighbor deserves a plain word before any paperwork goes to the committee. Halloween is Saturday, and decorations are welcome all week, so maybe there's room to talk about the birds instead of just tallying them. I'll greet her civilly, own up that I've been counting, and keep it dry. No sense repeating the warning I already gave.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna. I'll admit I've been standing here counting your flamingos, which is a poor way for a grown man to spend a Thursday. Halloween's Saturday, so tell me what you've got planned for them before I decide whether the committee needs to hear about it.

rosa.thought_process: I already handed in the parade cart folder and signed us up for Saturday's 6 PM parade. I'm on the bench resting my feet, nobody's around, and it's 8:17 PM. I've done what I came to do tonight. There's nothing left to push forward right now, so I'll take a few quiet minutes to breathe and run through Saturday's plan in my head before heading home: the clamps, the lights, the approval, and keeping every decoration visible and honest like we agreed.

parameters.content: Resting on the bench, going over Saturday's parade plan and enjoying the warm hazy evening before heading home.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
